Android Auto on the car screen

1. OvertakeLink is free, open-source software (GNU AGPL-3.0 license). You may use, study, modify and distribute it under the terms of that license.

2. The software is provided “as is”, without any warranty. You use it at your own risk. The authors are not liable for any damage — to your phone, head unit, car or data — or for consequences on the road.

3. Safety. Keep your eyes on the road. Set up OvertakeLink and Android Auto only while parked. Obey traffic rules.

4. OvertakeLink is an independent project and is not affiliated with Geely, Neusoft (QDLink) or Google. Names of these companies and their products are trademarks of their owners.

5. OvertakeLink uses the Android Auto developer mode. Google may change it at any time, and OvertakeLink may then stop working.

6. Data. OvertakeLink does not collect or send your data anywhere. The log is stored on your phone, and you share it yourself. The app contacts GitHub to check for and download updates.
Notifications — so OvertakeLink can run in the background with an icon in the status bar.\nMicrophone — for Android Auto voice commands.
Many phones (Xiaomi HyperOS and others) kill background apps.\nSet battery usage to “Unrestricted” and allow autostart, otherwise the connection to the car will drop.
Android Auto → tap the version number 10 times → ⋮ → “Start head unit server”.\nAfter a phone restart you may need to repeat this — OvertakeLink will remind you.

Connect the phone to the car’s USB port with a cable.
Android will ask which app should open “QDriveLink” — choose OvertakeLink and tick “Always”.
The first time, Android Auto will ask you on the phone to accept its terms and allow notification access — do it while parked.
It’s best to uninstall the stock QDLink app.
Bluetooth: audio and steering wheel buttons

Android Auto sound goes to the car over Bluetooth, just like your music does now. Make sure the phone is connected to the car.\nSteering wheel “next / previous” switch tracks while the head unit’s Bluetooth player is open. The voice button on the steering wheel is not supported yet — call the Assistant with “Hey Google” or the microphone icon on the car screen.
Use at your own risk: the app is provided “as is”, without warranty. Keep your eyes on the road — set everything up while parked.
OvertakeLink starts by itself when the car is connected with a cable and Android has asked which app to open it with.
Interface size, codec, audio and more are in the advanced settings of the built-in Android Auto receiver.
Compatible: the phone re-encodes the picture for the car screen. Slower, but works with any head unit.
Direct: the Android Auto picture goes to the car without re-encoding — lower latency, sharper, and the phone runs cooler.
If the car screen stays black in direct mode, try 720p, then 480p; if that doesn’t help, choose compatible. Applies the next time you plug in the cable.
